text.p: Salomon Brothers reiterated its "buy" recommendation on Finnish drugs wholesaler Tamro-yhtyma Oy after the company's 1996 results on Friday and said Tamro would have to expand in Denmark through acquisition.
"We like the stock," analyst Jeremy Green said by telephone from London, adding that it had good potential longer term.
He said Salomon's view was unchanged from a report reiterating the "buy", dated February 17 and received on Friday.
In that, Salomon said: "We believe the shares merit a 15-20 percent premium to European peers, rather than the current four percent, on normalised 1997 EPS."
Due to the difficulties Tamro experienced in Norway last year, Salomon said it was unlikely that the group would attempt to start a greenfield operation in Denmark.
"Tamro will therefore have to acquire either the publicly quoted Nomeco or one or both of the privately held Max Jenne or Tjellesen," Salomon said.
Although, Nomeco is publicly quoted it is very closely held with three shareholders holding 85.5 percent of share capital and 94.7 percent of votes, it added.
